items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: the band leader for the show was a female pianist named Ellie Frankel... when the show moved to Philadelphia they took her but she had to hire Philadelphia musicians.

ctx.x: So I kept in touch with Clark over the years and they had these competitive festivals in those days that were sponsored by DownBeat magazine and some of the tobacco or liquor companies. They had regional festivals. And the amazing thing was that the winners in different categories, like big band, small group, soloist, composer/arranger, and so on, of these regional festivals. And they had all their expenses paid to go to a national festival. And we were a national finalist two or three years before I moved on…

a couple of years. And in ’69 we got an invitation to play at the Montreux Jazz Festival in Switzerland. And the music school wouldn’t help us at all as far as raising money, you know, they weren’t interested in that at all. So the people that came to hear us down at Eddie’s, they found out about this, and they were so incensed by it that a bunch of the businessmen who came down to hear the band, they organized a whole series of fundraising concerts, and raised all the money to send the band to Switzerland. It’s…
